(1) the stress generation hypothesis is supported at the transdiagnostic level, (2) the specific stress generating effects of internalizing syndromes are limited to interpersonal dependent stress, and (3) the specific stress inhibition effects of panic disorder are limited to interpersonal stress.

stress generation is not a unitary phenomenon, but rather is a complex and multifactorial process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stress generation hypothesis can be expanded to include the effects of transdiagnostics pathology on stress generation, but that it is not a general explanation for the occurrence of all stressful life events.
, although the specific syndromes of anxiety and depression do not seem to be stress generators per se, their transdiagnostic dimensions may play a role in generating certain types of stress.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the stress generation model should be broadened to include transdiagnostic pathology, and that this transdiagnostic pathology should be modeled in terms of its unique and shared components.
stress generation models should not be limited to specific syndromes or even to specific diagnostic classes.
the transdiagnostic approach can be used to identify common and unique pathways through which different disorders contribute to stress generation.
